FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Brushware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. Although question may arise from some quarters about the term `BRUSH' as applied in this specification for the BRUSH RUBBER SQUEEZER for which the name `MOP' or `SQUEEGEE is better suited for the implement as per the usage in brushware industry. Following the age-old trade practice in this country, this specification has been titled as, Brushes, Rubber Squeezer, for a clear cut conception about the kind and type of the tool. Brushes, rubber squeezer are mainly used to swab, wipe or clear off water or small particles from flat surfaces like floors, platforms, ship decks, etc. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value of the specified value in this standard. this standard is complied of a test or analysis, shall numerical values ( revised)`. should be the same as that

1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for brushes, rubber squeezer. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards adjuncts to this standard:

4.1.2.2 The timber shall be reasonably straight grained and well seasoned to a moisture content not exceeding 15 percent when tested by moisture meter method. In case of dispute, the oven drying method shall be used ( see Annex B ). 4.1.2.3 The timber shall be free from brashness, any kind of biological or non-biological deterioration, insect attack, centre heart ( pith ), knots ( except live pin knots ), cracks, warp and any other defect which may reduce the life of the brush or affect its utility. 4.1.3 Nails

The rubber sheet shall remain unmovable inside the wooden block and shall not come out of it when subjected to a straight push and pull with thumb and finger grip. 4.5.2 Flexibility Test The rubber sheet when bent at an angle of 180" shall show no crack, split or break in the sheet. And on releasing the pressure while in bent, the sheet shall assume its normal shape.

Unless otherwise agreed to between the indentor or inspection authority and the supplier, each brush shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the following: a) Indication of the source of manufacture, and b) Month and year of manufacture. 6 SAMPLING The method of drawing representative of brushes and criteria for conformity as prescribed in Annex C. samples shall be

ANNEX

B

( Clause 4.1.2.2 )
DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT OF TIMBER USED IN BRUSHES, RUBBER SQUEEZER B-l TEST SPECIMEN B-I.1 The entire block used in brushes, rubber squeezer, may form the test specimen for the determination of moisture content or a coupon cut from the test specimen may, as well, be used for moisture content determination. When for any reason additional determination of moisture content is required, separate samples shall be prepared from the sample material as is used in preparing the test specimens. Smaller specimens-miy be &ed when deemed necessary. The test shall be carried out immediately after cutting the specimen. B-Z PROCEDURE B-2.1 Weigh accurately each test specimen. This specimen shal1 then be dried in a ventilated oven at 105" f 2�C until the mass becomes constant between two successive weighings made at an interval of not less than one hour. B-3 ~~~~~~~~~~~ B-3.1 Moisture content, percent by mass of oven-dry mass where w, = initial mass in g, of the test specimen; and w, = oven-dry mass, in g, of the test specimen.

SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY OF BRUSHES, RUBBER SQUEEZER C-l SAMPLES FOR APPROVAL C-l.1 The supplier shall submit three identical brushes corresponding to each type and size for approval. C-l.2 The purchaser or inspection authority, as applicable, shall retain one of the three samples. Alternatively, the following procedure may be adopted : Arrange the rubber squeezer brushes in some order, count them as 1, 2 ,......, up to r and so on where r is the integral part of N/n ( N being the lot size and n being the sample size). Repeating this process, every rth brush shall be withdrawn to constitute the sample. C-3 NUMBER OF TESTS FOR CONFORMITY AND CRITERIA

Standards

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by Details of conditions under BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
